trip.title: Toronto Thirteen Days
trip.bookingNote: Budget: food $500 minimum for the trip, more is better. Uber budget still to decide. Wagyu is a priority and has no venue picked yet.

places.name: Stay: St. James Town
places.notes: Sept 20-27. Sherbourne station, Line 2.

places.name: Stay: East End-Danforth
places.notes: Sept 27-Oct 2. Main Street station, Line 2.

places.name: ROSCon Global 2026
places.notes: Sheraton Centre. Sept 22-24.

places.name: Dual Citizen Coffee (Sheraton Centre)
places.notes: Host venue for the three NVIDIA daily meetups. Inside the Sheraton Centre, the same building as ROSCon, so there is no travel time. The organiser's own post asked "the same ROSCon Sheraton?", so find the exact spot in the lobby on day 1. Not the same as the unresolved Dual Citizen saved off Instagram (the one with the waterfall); confirm whether that is this location.

source.caption_excerpt: NVIDIA daily meetup at Dual Citizen Coffee Shop, Sheraton Centre

places.name: Post-ROSCon Hackathon
places.address: 65 King St E, Toronto, ON M5C 0C1
places.notes: Fri Sept 25, 09:30-17:30. King and Church, 10 min walk from the Sheraton. Hosted by Google / Intrinsic, so their guest security policy applies: the Luma registration must use your full legal name exactly as it appears on your passport, and you must bring the passport on the day. RSVP closes Mon Sept 21. Hacking on OSRF projects: ROS and ROS Control, Gazebo, Open-RMF, core infrastructure. Existing contributors welcome to come mentor.

booking.how: Registered via Luma, https://luma.com/vo6zoq5b, ticket in the event app. Shows as "You're Going". Before Sept 21, check the registered name is character-for-character what your passport says; Google / Intrinsic turn guests away on a name mismatch.

places.name: Scotiabank Arena
places.notes: Weezer Sept 25, Phoebe Bridgers Oct 1-2.

booking.how: Tickets already purchased. Check the door time on the ticket.

places.name: History

places.notes: At The Well, 2nd floor above Indigo.

places.name: Allan Gardens Conservatory
places.notes: Free Victorian greenhouse. Palms, cacti, orchids. Closes around 17:00.

source.caption_excerpt: One of the best free thing to do in Toronto

places.name: 10 Dean
places.notes: In the lobby of The Waverley. Contemporary art decor, strong matcha.

source.caption_excerpt: my new favorite WFH spot in downtown toronto

places.name: Ezra's Pound
places.notes: Retro coffee shop with a hidden back patio. Five minutes from Dupont station, on the way to Casa Loma.

source.caption_excerpt: found a secret patio + retro coffee shop

places.name: Zui Beer Bar
places.notes: Cyberpunk styling, Chinese street snacks, drink towers. DJs Fri and Sat from 21:00.

source.caption_excerpt: cyberpunk-inspired bar with Chinese street snacks

places.name: Nathan Phillips Square
places.notes: Directly across Queen St from the Sheraton. Two minutes from the ROSCon doors.

source.caption_excerpt: hot summer nights, mid-July

places.name: Yunnan Noodle Shack
places.notes: Solo-dining booths with panels you can fold away. Built for eating alone.

source.caption_excerpt: this unique concept for solo dining is an introverts dream

places.name: CIBC Square Park
places.notes: Elevated park above the rail corridor. Skyline and CN Tower, best at sunset.

source.caption_excerpt: 10/10 view in Toronnooooooo

places.name: Hanoi Bites
places.notes: Northern Vietnamese in Waterworks Food Hall. Banh mi and bun cha.

source.caption_excerpt: Finally Toronto coffee I can get behind

places.name: Roy Thomson Hall
places.notes: Photo spot. The trick from the reel: wait for a streetcar to cross the frame.

source.caption_excerpt: Roy Thompson hall is a super underrated location for a photo

places.name: Dear Darling
places.notes: Cocktail bar and kitchen. The "love bomb" is the one from the reel.

source.caption_excerpt: The love bomb drink only at Dear Darling

places.name: Toronto Music Garden
places.notes: Waterfront garden laid out to follow a Yo-Yo Ma cello suite. Walkable west along the water from the cruise dock.

source.caption_excerpt: designed around music

places.name: The Beaches
places.address: Queen St E at Lee Ave
places.notes: Boardwalk, lake, Queen St E shops. Ten minutes on foot from the east-end place.

source.caption_excerpt: this doesn't feel like Toronto and maybe that's why I love it

places.name: R.C. Harris Water Treatment Plant
places.notes: Art deco waterworks on the bluffs. Grounds open to the public, picnic and sunset spot.

source.caption_excerpt: my favorite picnic spot

places.name: Woodbine Beach
places.notes: Wide sand beach. Walk the boardwalk back east toward your place.

source.caption_excerpt: Woodbine Beach (Canada Day Fireworks)

places.name: Biidaasige Park
places.notes: Toronto’s largest new park in a generation, on the restored mouth of the Don. Wetlands, trails, ziplines. Two separate accounts flagged this one.

source.caption_excerpt: Toronto’s newest and largest park in a generation

places.name: Polson Pier
places.notes: Skyline across the harbour. Ten minutes from Biidaasige.

source.caption_excerpt: Polson Pier

places.name: Riverdale Park East
places.notes: The postcard skyline view from the east. Steep hill, worth it at sunset.

source.caption_excerpt: Summers in Toronto hit different

places.name: Cafe 85
places.notes: Brunch at Bay and Gerrard. The tiramisu french toast is the order; the reviewer was lukewarm on the roast beef benedict.

source.caption_excerpt: still thinking about this tiramisu french toast

places.name: Osgoode Hall
places.notes: Free. The Great Library is the reason to go, and it keeps restricted weekday hours, so check before turning up.

source.caption_excerpt: One of Toronto’s most beautiful buildings with a breathtaking library

places.name: 401 Richmond
places.notes: Galleries, artist studios, a bookstore and a public courtyard garden. Dark Horse Espresso inside. The open stairs are see-through.

source.caption_excerpt: home to galleries, artist studios, a bookstore, and even a hidden courtyard garden

places.name: University of Toronto, St George
places.notes: Walkable historic campus. Front and back campus are the photogenic parts.

source.caption_excerpt: UofT glaze

places.name: Acacia Cafe
places.notes: Inside Wycliffe College at UofT. Called a hidden gem in the reel.

source.caption_excerpt: 3 of my fav, most aesthetic cafés at uoft

places.name: Arbor Room, Hart House
places.notes: In Hart House at UofT. Hart House is generally open to the public.

source.caption_excerpt: 3 of my fav, most aesthetic cafés at uoft

places.name: Ace Hotel Toronto
places.notes: Shim-Sutcliffe building, RAIC Gold Medal 2021. Lobby cafe. Go for coffee, stay for the concrete.

source.caption_excerpt: go for the coffee and stay for the architecture

places.name: George Brown Waterfront library
places.notes: Lake-facing library. ACCESS UNCERTAIN: commenters could not agree whether non-students get in.

source.caption_excerpt: waterfront library

places.name: Jack Layton Ferry Terminal
places.notes: Ferry to the Islands. Cheap alternative to the CityPASS cruise, and the reel says the skyline is best on the ride BACK after dark.

source.caption_excerpt: the ride back at night gave me the most beautiful views

places.name: Dupont Station
places.notes: Tiled Line 1 station called the prettiest in the city. Walk north to the Baldwin Steps from here.

source.caption_excerpt: The prettiest subway station in Toronto

places.name: St. Patrick Station
places.notes: From a montage of TTC station architecture. Ride Line 1 and look up.

source.caption_excerpt: if St. Patrick had buskers and/or snacks she would be a 10

places.name: Financial District
places.address: King St W at Bay St
places.notes: Skyscraper canyon. Best at golden hour, and you walk through it daily during ROSCon anyway.

source.caption_excerpt: Toronto Is Giving Major NYC Energy

places.name: Sankofa Square (Yonge-Dundas Square)
places.notes: For pictures. Renamed from Yonge-Dundas Square in 2024. Big screens, busiest corner in the city. Right outside Eaton Centre.

places.name: Egg Club
places.notes: Goated spot. Breakfast. NOTE: picked the 531 Yonge storefront; there is also an Egg Club counter in the Union Station VIA concourse. Confirm which one you meant.

places.name: Yonge Street shops
places.address: Yonge St between Dundas and Wellesley
places.notes: Lots of stores. This is a strip, not a single address: pin anchored between Dundas and College, retail runs north from Eaton Centre.

places.name: Canada Computers
places.notes: Downtown store. Canada Computers runs three storefronts on this block of College (284, 343, 366); 366 is mainly A/V. Two blocks from Chinatown.

places.name: Memory Express
places.notes: Only location in the Toronto area, way out in Etobicoke near Sherway Gardens. About 25 min drive from downtown and roughly on the way to Mississauga: pair it with a Square One day rather than a downtown day.

places.name: Chinatown
places.address: Spadina Ave between Dundas and College
places.notes: Spadina strip. Walking distance to Canada Computers on College, Kensington Market, and Yunnan Noodle Shack.

places.name: Toronto Pearson (YYZ)
places.address: Toronto Pearson International Airport, Terminal 3, Mississauga, ON
places.notes: Flair flies out of Terminal 3. UP Express platform is at Terminal 1, LINK train between them.

places.name: UP Express (Union Station)
places.notes: Fast travel moment, 20 min. Union to Pearson, trains roughly every 15 min. Worth knowing for the Oct 2 departure.

places.name: Cactus Club Cafe
places.notes: Peach bellini. NOTE: picked the downtown Adelaide location; there is also one on The Queensway in Etobicoke, which would pair with Memory Express instead.

places.name: Milou
places.notes: Steak, in Little Portugal. French bistro, known for steak frites. CLOSED TUESDAY AND WEDNESDAY: has to land Thu-Mon.

places.name: Martin Goodman Trail (harbourfront)
places.address: Queens Quay W, at Harbourfront Centre
places.notes: Safe to bike, dedicated trail. Fully separated waterfront path. Pin is at Harbourfront Centre; the trail runs the whole waterfront east to the Beaches and west to Etobicoke.

places.name: Square One Shopping Centre
places.notes: Mississauga day, calmer than downtown Toronto. Biggest mall in Ontario. About 40 min by GO/MiWay from Union, or 30 min drive.

places.name: Simons (Square One)
places.notes: Inside Square One. Quebec department store, no Toronto-proper location, which is the reason to make the trip out.

places.name: Java-U Coffee House
places.notes: Flagged with a question mark. Nearest Java-U to Square One, about 10 min walk south of the mall. Verify this is the one you meant.

places.name: CF Toronto Eaton Centre
places.notes: Might be enough for shopping on its own. Connects by PATH; Sankofa Square is at its north door and the Yonge St shops run north from there.

places.name: Centre Island
places.notes: Ferry from Jack Layton Ferry Terminal, already on the shortlist as ferry-terminal. Skyline view back at the city. Bike rental on the island ties in with the trail idea.

booking.how: Toronto Island ferry tickets online ahead of time; queues are long on warm weekends.

places.name: Kill! Kill! Coffee
places.notes: New coffee spot on Dundas West.

places.name: Little Pebbles Cafe
places.notes: Viral creme brulee donuts, torched in front of you. Exclusive to the Baldwin St location.

places.name: Humble Donkey
places.notes: Best late-night laptop-friendly cafe. Patties supplied by Patty Cake.

places.name: AM Coffee Laboratory
places.notes: Toronto's first -86C dirty latte. Espresso poured over frozen distilled milk; you keep the glass jar.

places.name: 7 West Cafe
places.notes: Open 24/7. Old-school all-day breakfast, reliable late-night menu.

places.name: Mossop's Social
places.notes: Aesthetic cafe near Union Station.

places.notes: Aesthetic cafe near Union Station.

places.name: Mcha Bar

places.name: Butter Baker

places.name: Misfit Ice Cream

places.name: Sneaky Dee's

places.name: Firefly Burger

places.name: Taqueria el Pastorcito
places.notes: Authentic tacos: al pastor, lengua. Fri-Sat 12pm-4am.

places.name: HanBingo
places.notes: Korean dessert cafe, fluffy bingsu shaved ice. Thu-Sun until 4am.

places.name: Alexandros Take Out
places.notes: Greek gyros and souvlaki. Fast, big portions. Fri-Sat 11am-4am.

places.name: Rap's
places.notes: Jamaican. Jerk chicken, oxtail, curry goat. Tue-Sun 10am-3am.

places.name: Oklahoma Burgers
places.notes: Billed as the best burger in Toronto.

places.name: Gloria in the Great Hall
places.notes: Coziest brunch spot, known for french toast. Martini happy hour 5-7PM, open late. Brunch through date night.

places.name: Cafe Polonez

places.name: Moon Milk

places.name: Bang Bang Ice Cream
places.notes: 1000/10. London fog and mango are standouts. Expect a line on Friday nights.

places.name: Brickhouse Waffle
places.notes: Rated 6/10 in the reel: matcha flavour kinda mid, egg waffle not crispy enough. Low priority.

places.name: Pizzeria Badiali
places.notes: Ossington Friday night staple. Parking is brutal, walk or transit.

places.name: Paris Paris
places.notes: Wine bar on the Ossington strip, good around 9pm.

places.name: Ghazale
places.notes: Huge portions, sweet staff. Chicken shawarma plate and falafel wrap. Local chain.

places.name: Mirello Tiramisu & Gelato
places.notes: Toronto's first pay-by-weight tiramisu. $9/100g tiramisu, $5.50/100g gelato. No scoop-backs, so go easy.

places.name: Civil Liberties

places.name: Future

places.name: Vertigo Toronto
places.notes: After-hours house and techno. Weekends until 7am, hours vary by event.

places.name: Twister Karaoke

places.name: Rendezviews

places.notes: Must-try: cheesecake.

places.name: Le Genie Bakery & Espresso

places.name: Aux Merveilleux de Fred
places.notes: Must-try: vergeoise waffle.

places.name: Castle & Coal
places.notes: Must-try: Ontario roasted corn kouign amann.

places.name: Dear Grain
places.notes: Must-try: multigrain porridge pan loaf.

places.name: Queen's Park
places.notes: Canada's first municipal park. Walkable from UofT and Yorkville.

places.name: Grange Park
places.notes: Owned by the AGO. Pair it with an AGO visit.

places.name: Christie Pits Park
places.notes: Ball diamond, volleyball court, outdoor amenities.

places.name: Trinity Bellwoods Park
places.notes: Largest park in downtown Toronto's core.

places.name: Trillium Park
places.notes: 1200 trees and 28,000 shrubs planted during development. Free.

places.name: High Park
places.notes: Runs nature clubs for all ages. Free. Toronto's big west-end park.

places.name: Spadina Museum
places.notes: Start a 24h Toronto itinerary here. Next door to Casa Loma.

places.name: Ossington Avenue
places.notes: One of Toronto's coolest neighbourhoods. Bars, pizza, ice cream. Best on a Friday night, and parking is impossible.

places.name: Scarborough Bluffs
places.notes: 90m cliffs, beach, hiking. 45-60 min from downtown: subway to Kennedy then bus 201. Swim, hike, kayak, best sunset views.

places.name: Guild Park and Gardens
places.notes: Collection of architectural relics salvaged from demolished downtown Toronto buildings, including the Greek Theatre from the old Bank of Toronto.

places.name: Distillery District
places.notes: Free to wander. Cobblestone pedestrian streets.

places.name: Graffiti Alley
places.notes: Free. Just south of Queen West, runs parallel to it.

places.name: Kensington Market
places.notes: Kensington on a Sunday is free therapy. Car-free on Pedestrian Sundays.

places.name: St. Lawrence Market
places.notes: Closed Mondays. Fri hours run to 19:00. Peameal bacon sandwich is the classic order.

places.name: Gooderham Building
places.notes: The flatiron. Classic photo looking east down Wellington.

places.name: Stackt Market
places.notes: Free. Shipping container market, rotating vendors and events.

places.name: HTO Park
places.notes: Free. Urban beach with yellow umbrellas on the waterfront.

places.name: Humber Bay Arch Bridge
places.notes: Free. On the Martin Goodman Trail, good sunrise and skyline shots.

places.name: Aga Khan Museum
places.notes: FREE every Wednesday 4-8pm.

places.name: Toronto Railway Museum
places.notes: Right at the base of the CN Tower in Roundhouse Park.

places.name: Little Canada
places.notes: Miniature Canada exhibit, right on the Yonge strip.

places.name: Evergreen Brick Works
places.notes: Former quarry turned park and market. Saturday farmers market.

places.name: Little Italy
places.notes: College St strip. Ghazale and Sneaky Dee's are both here.

places.name: Kew Beach
places.notes: In the Beaches, next to Woodbine.

places.name: Ward's Island
places.notes: Quieter island than Centre. Ferry from the same terminal.

places.name: Hanlan's Point
places.notes: Best $9 in Toronto: take the ferry from Hanlan's back to Harbourfront at NIGHT for the iconic skyline view.

places.name: Exhibition Place
places.notes: Grounds of the CNE.

places.name: Hart House
places.notes: Candlelight concerts here. Arbor Room cafe is inside.

places.name: Trinity College, UofT
places.notes: The Hogwarts one. Stone archways, ivy walls, quiet courtyards. Best early morning or golden hour, fewer people. Combine with Queen's Park and Yorkville.

places.name: Toronto Reference Library
places.notes: Free. Big atrium, good quiet stop off Yonge.

places.name: Downsview Park
places.notes: WATER LANTERN FESTIVAL Sept 18-20 2026: gates 4:30pm, lantern launch 7:30-8:30pm, food trucks and music. NOTE: ends two days before you land.

places.name: Paradise Theatre
places.notes: Live shows and repertory cinema.

places.name: Sherway Gardens
places.notes: Euro summer hack if you're stuck in Toronto. Close to Memory Express, on the way to Mississauga.

places.name: Acadia Art & Rare Books
places.notes: Secret vintage bookstore with two resident cats, Frodo and Pippin. Rare books and antiques. Browse the collection online first.

places.name: Toronto Zoo
places.notes: Far northeast, a half-day commitment.

places.name: Horseshoe Falls
places.notes: The main event. Free to look at from the Niagara Parkway railing; everything else here is paid.

places.name: Table Rock Welcome Centre
places.notes: Closest building to the brink of the falls. Food court, washrooms, and the entrance to Journey Behind the Falls.

places.name: Niagara Takes Flight
places.address: Table Rock Centre, Niagara Falls, ON
places.notes: Immersive flying theatre over 56km of parkland. Adult $33, child $21.50, allow about 30 min. Timed ticket.

places.name: Journey Behind the Falls
places.address: Table Rock Centre, Niagara Falls, ON
places.notes: Tunnels cut behind the falls plus a lower observation deck. Bundled with the boat ride and tower from about $39.

places.name: Niagara City Cruises
places.notes: The boat into the mist, the one everyone photographs. Evening fireworks cruise is about $54 for 40 min. You will get wet.

booking.how: Book a time slot online, queues are long.

places.name: Skylon Tower
places.notes: Observation deck and a revolving restaurant. Tower plus Journey Behind the Falls bundles around $88; the buffet runs about $120.

places.name: White Water Walk
places.notes: Brand new viewing platform as of 2026. Descend 70m into the gorge to a 305m boardwalk beside Class 6 whirlpool rapids running up to 48km/h. 4km north of the falls.

places.name: Whirlpool Aero Car
places.notes: Antique cable car strung across the whirlpool. Next door to White Water Walk, so pair them.

places.name: Niagara SkyWheel
places.notes: About $17 for an 8 min ride. Best after dark when the falls are lit.

places.name: Clifton Hill
places.notes: The loud tourist strip: arcades, wax museums, neon. Cheesy on purpose. Walk it once after dinner.

places.name: Niagara Falls Bus Terminal
places.notes: Where GO and coach services arrive. WEGO shuttle connects it to the falls.

items.title: Breakfast at YWG before boarding
items.notes: Flight is 09:25, so eat landside early.

items.title: Flight F8642 departs YWG
items.notes: Winnipeg 09:25, 2h30m.

items.title: Land YYZ Pearson
items.notes: Terminal 3 for Flair. Allow 30 min for bags.
Lunch at Pearson, Terminal 3. Eat before the UP Express rather than hunting for food with luggage.
UP Express from Pearson, 25 min, trains every 15. Buy on the app. Then down to Line 1 for Bloor.
Check in. Confirm your real arrival time.
12 min walk. Free, and it closes around 17:00 so go straight there.
Sunday hours are short, usually 11:00-19:00, so this is the one evening slot that works. PATH connects it back toward the hotel.
Dinner. Easy first night food, open late.
Two minutes from dinner, at the Eaton Centre north door. Big screens, best after dark.
Browse north from Sankofa. Sunday evening: most stores will be shut, so treat this as a walk, not shopping.
Open 24/7 at Yonge & Bloor, and on the way back to St. James Town. The reliable late stop on a night when everything else has closed.
Back at the apartment.

advice.title: Pad every TTC trip by 20 minutes
advice.body: Local advice, repeated often: leave 20 minutes earlier than the TTC app tells you to. Streetcars bunch and short-turn.

advice.title: Learn the PATH
advice.body: 27km of underground walkway links Union, the Financial District, Eaton Centre and the Sheraton Centre. Useful for your ROSCon days if it rains.

advice.title: UP Express beats a cab to Pearson
advice.body: Union to Pearson in about 25 minutes, trains roughly every 15. Fixed fare, no traffic risk. This is how you get to your Oct 2 flight.

advice.title: Free museum windows
advice.body: ROM is free the third Tuesday of the month, 5:30-8:30pm. Aga Khan Museum is free every Wednesday 4-8pm. Neither lands conveniently in your dates, but worth checking on arrival.

advice.title: Arcadia Earth student discount
advice.body: 50% off tickets with a valid college or university student ID, running until Oct 31 2026. Covers your whole trip.

advice.title: Buy island ferry tickets online
advice.body: Buy direct from the ferry website rather than queueing at the terminal. The line is routinely longer than the crossing itself.

advice.title: Apps locals actually use
advice.body: Too Good To Go for 50-75% off restaurant food near closing. Fever for one-off events. SpotHero to pre-book downtown parking. ClassPass gives 4-10 free classes on a first signup.

advice.title: Skip the rooftop queue
advice.body: The rooftop is never worth the wait; the street-side patio is better and you get seated. Applies to most of King West and Ossington.

advice.title: Summerlicious and Winterlicious
advice.body: Prix fixe promotions that put expensive kitchens within reach. Summerlicious runs in July and Winterlicious in late January, so neither hits your dates, but it is why some 'best of' lists look cheaper than reality.

advice.title: Kensington Market on a Sunday
advice.body: Called free therapy locally. Car-free Pedestrian Sundays make it a different place. Sept 20 and 27 are both Sundays on your trip.

advice.title: Islands ferry lines peak midday
advice.body: Go early or go at night. The night crossing from Hanlan's Point back to Harbourfront is the single best skyline view in the city and costs about $9.

advice.title: Nature is closer than it looks
advice.body: Scarborough Bluffs is 45-60 minutes by subway to Kennedy then bus 201: 90m cliffs, beach and hiking. High Park, the waterfront trail and the Beaches are all inside the city.

advice.title: Construction is constant
advice.body: Toronto has more active cranes than any other city in North America. Expect closed sidewalks and detours, especially downtown. Another reason for the 20-minute padding.

advice.title: Cheap late-night is a real category
advice.body: Sneaky Dee's until 3am, 7 West Cafe 24/7, Firefly Burger and Future until 4am on weekends. Useful after the Weezer, Malcolm Todd and Phoebe Bridgers shows.

advice.title: No weekday GO train to Niagara any more
advice.body: Metrolinx cut three of the five weekday Niagara train trips on 8 Sept 2026, running through to spring 2027. The two survivors are commuter-direction only: Niagara to Union at 06:36, Union to Niagara at 16:59. Weekday travel means a Lakeshore West train to Burlington then GO bus Route 12B. Most travel blogs and aggregators still quote the old three-a-day service, so trust only the current Metrolinx PDF or trip planner.

advice.title: Take the 12B express, never the local 12
advice.body: Both leave Burlington at :58 past the hour. The 12B express does Burlington to Niagara Falls in 50 minutes; the local Route 12 takes 80. On the way back the 20:57 express and the 20:31 local both reach Union at 23:15, so the express buys you 26 extra minutes at the falls for free.

advice.title: Fireworks at 22:00, and the last bus home
advice.body: Niagara Parks runs fireworks nightly at 22:00 through 12 October, and falls illumination starts at 20:00 from 19 September. Staying for the fireworks means the 22:27 bus, the LAST GO connection of the night, reaching Union at 00:50. Book a taxi in advance for the hop from Table Rock to the Bus Terminal: the walk is 2km through the departing crowd, and missing that bus means an unplanned hotel night.

advice.title: GO+WEGO combo ticket
advice.body: About $34 return on a weekday, bundling the GO trip with unlimited WEGO in Niagara. Worth it: the GO station sits roughly 2km from Horseshoe Falls and the attractions are spread along the Parkway. WEGO Green Line runs every 15-20 min, last buses around 23:10.

advice.title: Passport for the Friday hackathon
advice.body: The post-ROSCon hackathon is hosted at the Google / Intrinsic Toronto office and their guest policy has no flexibility: register in Luma under your full legal name exactly as it appears on your passport, and carry the passport on Sept 25. Check the registered name now rather than on the day, and note RSVPs close Mon Sept 21.
